family_title: Multiplicative, Orthogonal, Scaling & Spectral Methods (group and monoid actions on W_0)

methods.name: OFT
methods.paper_title: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion by Orthogonal Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 R,\quad R = \operatorname{diag}(R_1,\dots,R_r)\in O(d_{in}),\ R_i = (I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i=-Q_i^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b},\ b=d_{in}/r;\ \text{COFT: } \|R-I\|\le\epsilon;\ W_0 \text{ frozen, } \{Q_i\} \text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear / conv layer (originally the attention projections of the Stable Diffusion UNet); acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of the block-diagonal orthogonal subgroup O(b)^r < O(d_in) on W_0 (paper writes z=(R W^0)^T x with W^0 of shape d_in x d_out; in the h=Wx convention this is W = W_0 R^T, and R^T ranges over the same group). Every neuron (row of W_0) is rotated by the same R, so all pairwise neuron angles and the hyperspherical energy are invariants; R is reached through the Cayley chart from the Lie algebra so(b)^r.
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 R is a dense matrix of the original shape that can be computed once and stored in place of W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0 gives R = I, so the model is exactly the pretrained one at initialization.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune by rotating all neurons of a layer with one shared orthogonal matrix. This keeps the angles between pretrained neurons (their hyperspherical energy), which the paper argues carries the semantic information. A block-diagonal R keeps the parameter count low.
methods.results_note: On Stable Diffusion subject-driven and controllable generation, OFT/COFT is reported to beat existing fine-tuning methods in generation quality and convergence speed.

relations.note: OFT with r blocks of size b is BOFT(1,b); BOFT(1,d) is unconstrained OFT
OFT saves parameters with a sparse block-diagonal multiplicative structure where LoRA uses a low-rank additive one (128x128 example: OFT r=8 needs 960 vs LoRA r=8 2048 parameters)
same function class (block-diagonal orthogonal right action on W_0); OFTv2 evaluates it on the input and approximates the Cayley inverse with a Neumann series

methods.name: BOFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Orthogonal Finetuning via Butterfly Factorization
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 R(m,b),\quad R(m,b)=\prod_{i=1}^{m}\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)},\ \big(\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)}\big)^{\top}\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)}=I,\ \text{each factor a permuted block-diagonal matrix of } b\times b \text{ Cayley-parameterized orthogonal blocks};\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.locus: any linear / conv layer (attention and MLP of ViTs, LLMs, SAM, Stable Diffusion); acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of a product of m sparse butterfly factors, each a permutation conjugate of the block-diagonal subgroup O(b)^{d/b}; the product is a dense orthogonal matrix. The paper frames this as information transmission on a butterfly grid graph (a Cooley-Tukey style factorization of an O(d) element).
methods.mergeable_reason: The product R(m,b) is a fixed orthogonal matrix after training, so W_0 R can be precomputed.
methods.identity_at_init: All skew-symmetric generators start at 0, so every butterfly factor is the identity and R = I.
methods.key_idea: Build a dense orthogonal matrix as a product of sparse butterfly-structured orthogonal factors. OFT then gets dense rotations from O(d log d) parameters. Block-diagonal OFT is the m=1 case.
methods.results_note: Reports higher scores than LoRA and OFT on GLUE (DeBERTaV3), the best VTAB-1K average (77.9%), stronger LLaMA-7B MMLU results, HQ-SAM-level segmentation with 3% of its parameters, and better controllable and subject-driven Stable Diffusion generation.

relations.note: BOFT(1,b) is block-diagonal OFT; BOFT(1,d) is full OFT
both build O(d) elements from log-depth sparse factors; GOFT uses one Givens angle per pair and fewer pairs per layer
multiplicative sparse factorization in place of low-rank addition

methods.name: OFTv2
methods.full_name: Orthogonal Finetuning v2 (input-centric OFT with Cayley-Neumann parameterization; QOFT for quantized models)
methods.paper_title: Orthogonal Finetuning Made Scalable
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0\,(R\,x),\quad R=\operatorname{diag}(R_1,\dots,R_r),\ R_i=(I+Q_i)\Big(I+\sum_{k=1}^{K}Q_i^{k}\Big)\approx(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i=-Q_i^{\top};\ \text{QOFT: } h=\mathrm{Dequant}(W_q)\,(R\,x);\ W_0 \text{ (or } W_q) \text{ frozen}
methods.locus: any linear layer (input activations are rotated before the frozen matmul); works on top of quantized base weights
methods.structure: the same block-diagonal (now only approximately) orthogonal action as OFT, evaluated as an action on the input vector x (two matrix-vector products, O(nd + d^2)) instead of on W_0 (matrix-matrix, O(nd^2)). The truncated Neumann series makes the Cayley map only approximately orthogonal.
methods.mergeable_reason: For a full-precision base, R can be folded into W_0 (W_0 R); for QOFT, merging requires re-quantizing the merged weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0 gives R = I.
methods.key_idea: Rotate the input instead of the weight, which cuts OFT's cost from cubic to quadratic. Replace the matrix inverse in the Cayley transform with a truncated Neumann series. Because R acts on activations, the method runs on any quantized backbone (QOFT).
methods.results_note: Reports up to 10x faster training and 3x lower GPU memory than the original OFT, and better results than QLoRA when fine-tuning quantized Qwen2.5 models (0.5B-72B) for math reasoning; also applied to Stable Diffusion 3.5.

relations.note: same group action; input-centric evaluation and Cayley-Neumann approximation
QOFT targets the same quantized-base setting as QLoRA

methods.name: HRA
methods.paper_title: Bridging The Gap between Low-rank and Orthogonal Adaptation via Householder Reflection Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 H^{(r)},\quad H^{(r)}=\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Big(I-2\tfrac{u_iu_i^{\top}}{\|u_i\|^2}\Big)=I+U_r\Gamma_rU_r^{\top},\ u_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}};\ \text{loss}+\lambda\sum_{l}\big\|I_r-U_r^{(l)\top}U_r^{(l)}\big\|_F^2;\ W_0 \text{ frozen, } U_r=[u_1,\dots,u_r] \text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (LLM attention/MLP projections, Stable Diffusion attention); acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of a word of length r in Householder reflections (an element of O(d_in) that differs from I by a rank<=r matrix). W_0 H = W_0 + (W_0 U_r Gamma_r) U_r^T, so it is an orthogonal multiplicative update and an adaptive rank-r additive update at the same time. The regularizer lambda moves between free reflections (lambda=0) and Gram-Schmidt-orthonormal reflection planes (lambda -> infinity).
methods.mergeable_reason: H^(r) is a fixed d_in x d_in matrix after training, so W_0 H^(r) can be precomputed.
methods.identity_at_init: The reflection vectors are initialized in identical pairs (u_{2i-1} = u_{2i}), so consecutive reflections cancel and H^(r) = I. This needs even r (default in HF PEFT; odd r falls back to random init with a warning).
methods.key_idea: A chain of r learnable Householder reflections is an orthogonal matrix and also the identity plus a rank-r term. HRA is therefore both orthogonal fine-tuning and adaptive low-rank adaptation. A penalty on how far the reflection planes are from orthogonal trades capacity against regularity.
methods.results_note: Reports better performance than LoRA, OFT and BOFT variants with fewer trainable parameters on GLUE, LLaMA-2 math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH) and Stable Diffusion subject-driven/controllable generation.

relations.note: orthogonal right action on W_0, generated by reflections instead of Cayley blocks
the paper shows W_0 H^(r) = W_0 + A(W_0,B)B, an adaptive rank-r LoRA whose left factor depends on W_0

a block-diagonal ETHER with n blocks equals a product of n Householder reflections whose vectors have disjoint supports, i.e. HRA with r=n mutually orthogonal u_i (HRA also makes the identity reachable by pairing)

methods.name: GOFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter Efficient Quasi-Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Givens Rotation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 R^{\top},\quad R=\prod_{\ell=1}^{\log_2 d_{in}}P_\ell,\ P_\ell=\prod_{k=0}^{d_{in}/2^{\ell}-1}G\big(2^{\ell}k,\ 2^{\ell-1}(2k+1);\ \theta_k^{\ell}\big),\ G(i,j;\theta) \text{ a Givens rotation in the } (i,j) \text{ plane};\ W_0 \text{ frozen, angles } \theta \text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of SO(d_in), with the group element written as a product of d-1 Givens rotations (one-parameter subgroups SO(2) embedded in coordinate planes) arranged in log2(d) parallel layers of non-overlapping rotations, a butterfly-like layout
methods.mergeable_reason: The product of Givens rotations is a fixed orthogonal matrix that can be multiplied into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: All angles start at 0 (each rotation initialized to the identity).
methods.key_idea: d-1 Givens rotations can map any vector to any other vector on the same sphere, so OFT-level expressiveness only needs O(d) angles instead of O(d^2) parameters. A parallel arrangement keeps the depth at O(log d) sequential layers.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with DeBERTaV3-base, GOFT with 0.08M parameters matches OFT (b=8, 0.66M parameters) at an 88.78 average; also evaluated on LLaMA-2-7B instruction tuning and VTAB-1K.

relations.note: same orthogonal right action; far sparser parameterization
up to permutation conventions, a sparser instance of BOFT(log d, 2): butterfly layer l keeps only d/2^l of its d/2 2x2 rotations active and fixes the rest to the identity
qGOFT relaxes each Givens block to a general 2x2 matrix

methods.name: qGOFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter Efficient Quasi-Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Givens Rotation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0\tilde{R}^{\top},\quad \tilde{R}=\prod_{\ell}\tilde{P}_\ell,\ \text{each Givens block replaced by a free } \tilde{G}_i=[\alpha_i\ \beta_i]\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2};\ \min\ \mathcal{L}+\lambda\sum_i\langle\alpha_i,\beta_i\rangle^2;\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of a product of embedded GL(2) blocks laid out like GOFT. Leaving SO(d) lets the update change neuron norms and angles, and a soft column-orthogonality penalty keeps it near the orthogonal group.
methods.mergeable_reason: The product of 2x2 blocks is a fixed matrix that can be multiplied into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Every quasi-Givens block is initialized to the 2x2 identity.
methods.key_idea: Relax each Givens rotation to an arbitrary 2x2 linear map, so fine-tuning can also rescale neurons and shift their angles. A soft regularizer keeps the map close to orthogonal.
methods.results_note: Reports an 89.35 GLUE average on DeBERTaV3-base with 0.33M parameters (above OFT b=8 with 0.66M) and a 79.4% VTAB-1K average.

relations.note: Givens rotations relaxed to general 2x2 blocks with a soft orthogonality penalty
both act with 2x2 blocks; RoAd uses scaled rotations on output coordinate pairs

methods.name: ETHER
methods.paper_title: ETHER: Efficient Finetuning of Large-Scale Models with Hyperplane Reflections
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 H^{B},\quad H^{B}=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\dots,H_n),\ H_j=I-2u_ju_j^{\top},\ \|u_j\|=1,\ u_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}/n};\ \|H_j-I\|_F=2;\ W_0 \text{ frozen, } u_j \text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (diffusion attention, LLM projections); acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of a block-diagonal product of n hyperplane reflections, an element of O(d_in) that lies at fixed distance ||H_j - I||_F = 2 from the identity in every block
methods.mergeable_reason: H^B is a fixed orthogonal matrix that can be multiplied into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exactly: a Householder reflection is never the identity, so the model is moved at step 0 by a bounded, fixed-size transformation. Training only re-orients the reflection hyperplanes. Exact initialization details were not confirmed in the text read.
methods.key_idea: Restricting the multiplicative update to hyperplane reflections bounds how far the fine-tuned weights can move from the pretrained ones, whatever the learning rate. The result needs very few parameters and is robust to hyperparameters.
methods.results_note: Reports performance matching or beating LoRA and OFT with about 10-100x fewer parameters on subject-driven and controllable Stable Diffusion generation, GLUE and LLaMA instruction tuning.

relations.note: block-diagonal orthogonal action with each block restricted to a single reflection

diag(H_1,...,H_n) is a product of n reflections with disjoint-support vectors, i.e. HRA with r=n orthogonal reflection vectors and without the identity-preserving pairing (the two methods were concurrent)

methods.name: ETHER+
methods.full_name: ETHER+ (relaxed two-hyperplane transformation applied on both sides)
methods.paper_title: ETHER: Efficient Finetuning of Large-Scale Models with Hyperplane Reflections
methods.formula_latex: W=\tilde{H}^{+}\,W_0\,H^{+},\quad H^{+}=I-uu^{\top}+vv^{\top}\ (u,v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}}\ \text{unit, block-diagonal}),\ \tilde{H}^{+}=I-\tilde u\tilde u^{\top}+\tilde v\tilde v^{\top}\ (\tilde u,\tilde v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}});\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on both the input and the output side of W_0
methods.structure: two-sided action (left on R^{d_out}, right on R^{d_in}) by rank<=2 perturbations of the identity. These are not orthogonal in general, so they leave the group O(d), but their distance to I is bounded by ETHER's.
methods.mergeable_reason: Both transforms are fixed matrices after training, so H~+ W_0 H+ can be precomputed.
methods.identity_at_init: H+ = I when u = v, so unlike ETHER the identity can be represented. Whether the released code initializes u = v was not confirmed.
methods.key_idea: Relax the Householder reflection to I - uu^T + vv^T so that two hyperplanes can interact or cancel. Applied on both sides of W_0, this gives finer, still norm-bounded updates.
methods.results_note: Reports e.g. 0.666 DINO for subject-driven generation with 0.4M parameters vs OFT's 0.652 with 11.6M, and 27.3 mIoU vs 24.5 for controllable generation.

relations.note: a two-hyperplane relaxation of the reflection that can reach the identity
DeLoRA is derived from ETHER+ by making the bound on the deviation learnable and the rank arbitrary

methods.name: PSOFT
methods.paper_title: Efficient Orthogonal Fine-Tuning with Principal Subspace Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_{res}+B\,\operatorname{diag}(\beta)\,R\,\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\,A,\quad W_0=W_{res}+BA,\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{row-orthonormal},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{(top-}r\text{ SVD of } W_0\text{, frozen)};\ R\in O(r)\ \text{(Cayley-Neumann)},\ \alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\ \text{trained};\ \alpha=\beta=\mathbf{1}\Rightarrow W=W_0\big(I+A^{\top}(R-I)A\big)
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on the principal input subspace of W_0
methods.structure: OFT restricted to the r-dimensional principal input subspace. O(r) acts on W_0 from the right through the embedding R -> I + A^T(R-I)A in O(d_in), which is the identity on the orthogonal complement. Two diagonal scalings (alpha, beta) gradually relax exact orthogonality.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapted weight W_res + B diag(beta) R diag(alpha) A is a fixed dense matrix after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0 (so R = I) and alpha = beta = 1 give W = W_0 exactly.
methods.key_idea: Confine orthogonal fine-tuning to the principal subspace of W_0 found by SVD. An r x r rotation plus two tunable scaling vectors then preserves the subspace geometry the way OFT does, with LoRA-like memory and far fewer parameters.
methods.results_note: Across 35 NLP/CV tasks and four backbones, avoids the out-of-memory failures of OFT/BOFT/qGOFT, gives up to 18x higher parameter efficiency on DeBERTaV3 GLUE, the best VTAB-1K average (73.4%), +2.28% over LoRA on LLaMA-3.2-3B GSM8K and +1.4% average on LLaMA-3.1-8B commonsense reasoning.

relations.note: orthogonal action restricted to a principal subspace
uses the Cayley-Neumann parameterization
with alpha=beta=1, PSOFT is mathematically a one-sided (right) Spectral Adapter^R: a rotation of the top-r right singular subspace
principal-subspace (top singular) factors of W_0 obtained by SVD

methods.name: Spectral Adapter^R
methods.paper_title: Spectral Adapter: Fine-Tuning in Spectral Space
methods.formula_latex: W=[U_1R_U,\ U_2]\,S\,[V_1R_V,\ V_2]^{\top}=\tilde{U}\,W_0\,\tilde{V}^{\top},\quad \tilde{U}=I+U_1(R_U-I)U_1^{\top},\ \tilde{V}=I+V_1(R_V-I)V_1^{\top};\ W_0=USV^{\top}\ \text{frozen},\ R_U,R_V\in O(r)\ \text{(Cayley) trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (top-r spectral space of each pretrained weight)
methods.structure: two-sided orthogonal action of O(r) x O(r), embedded in O(d_out) x O(d_in) as rotations of the top-r left and right singular subspaces of W_0 (identity on their complements). Singular values are unchanged and only the principal singular frames are rotated.
methods.mergeable_reason: The rotated singular factors recombine into one dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: R_U = R_V = I.
methods.key_idea: Run the SVD of each pretrained weight and fine-tune only by rotating its top singular vectors. The adapter is very compact, and keeping the adapted subspaces orthogonal helps when several adapters are fused.

relations.note: OFT-style orthogonal action restricted to the principal spectral subspace
same paper; rotational vs additive tuning of the top singular vectors

methods.name: Spectral Adapter^A
methods.paper_title: Spectral Adapter: Fine-Tuning in Spectral Space
methods.formula_latex: W=[U_1+A_U,\ U_2]\,S\,[V_1+A_V,\ V_2]^{\top},\quad A_U\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_V\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{trained};\ W_0=USV^{\top}\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: any linear layer (top-r singular vectors)
methods.structure: additive perturbation of the top-r singular-vector factors: Delta W = A_U S_1 V_1^T + U_1 S_1 A_V^T + A_U S_1 A_V^T. This has rank <= 2r for LoRA's parameter budget (the paper's 'twice the rank capacity' lemma).
methods.mergeable_reason: The perturbed factors recombine into a single dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: A_U = A_V = 0.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune the top singular vectors of the pretrained weight additively. For the same number of trainable parameters this doubles LoRA's rank capacity and uses the pretrained spectrum.
methods.results_note: Reports 49.73 on GSM8K with Llama-3-8B vs 44.81 for LoRA, and an 88.03 GLUE average on DeBERTaV3-base, above LoRA, DoRA and OFT.

relations.note: same parameter budget, twice the rank capacity
both adapt the principal singular subspace of W_0 (concurrent work)
same paper; additive vs rotational

methods.name: SVDiff
methods.paper_title: SVDiff: Compact Parameter Space for Diffusion Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W=U\,\operatorname{diag}\big(\mathrm{ReLU}(\sigma+\delta)\big)\,V^{\top},\quad W_0=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)V^{\top}\ \text{(SVD, frozen)},\ \delta\in\mathbb{R}^{\min(d_{in},d_{out})}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: conv and linear weight kernels of the diffusion UNet (cross-attention layers matter most); optionally the text encoder
methods.structure: the singular values are adjusted by a diagonal (torus) map while the singular vectors stay fixed. For sigma > 0 this equals W = U diag(s/sigma) U^T W_0 with s = ReLU(sigma+delta) >= 0, a positive-semidefinite rescaling that commutes with W_0 W_0^T.
methods.mergeable_reason: U diag(ReLU(sigma+delta)) V^T is a fixed dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: delta = 0.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune only the singular values of every weight matrix (spectral shifts). The tiny parameter space resists overfitting in personalization and supports multi-subject training (Cut-Mix-Unmix) and single-image editing (CoSINE).
methods.results_note: About 1.7MB of parameters for Stable Diffusion vs 3.66GB for full DreamBooth (roughly 2,200x smaller) and 1/2-1/3 of a LoRA checkpoint.

relations.note: SVF scales singular values multiplicatively; SVDiff shifts them additively (equivalent reparameterizations for sigma > 0)
SVFT with a diagonal mask is a spectral shift without the ReLU
much smaller checkpoint for diffusion personalization

methods.name: SVF (Transformer²)
methods.paper_title: Transformer-Squared: Self-adaptive LLMs
methods.formula_latex: W=U\big(\Sigma\otimes\operatorname{diag}(z)\big)V^{\top}=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma\odot z)V^{\top}\ \Big(\times\tfrac{\sum_i\sigma_i}{\sum_i\sigma_iz_i}\ \text{in the official code}\Big),\quad W_0=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)V^{\top}\ \text{frozen},\ z\in\mathbb{R}^{\min(d_{in},d_{out})}\ \text{trained (REINFORCE + KL)};\ \text{test time: } z'=\sum_k\alpha_kz_k
methods.locus: weight matrices of the LLM (the official code adapts the MLP matrices)
methods.structure: multiplicative diagonal (torus) action on the singular values with fixed singular vectors. Trained expert vectors z_k can be linearly mixed at inference.
methods.mergeable_reason: Once z (or the mixture z') is chosen, W is a fixed dense matrix; self-adaptation is a two-pass procedure that sets z before the second pass.
methods.identity_at_init: z starts near a constant value (the paper's hyperparameter table lists an initial mean of 0.1). The official code passes z through a sigmoid and renormalizes by sum(sigma)/sum(sigma*z), so a uniform z leaves W_0 unchanged up to this normalization (approximately the identity).
methods.key_idea: Train one scaling vector over each weight's singular values with RL to get compact, composable 'expert' vectors. At test time a dispatcher identifies the task and mixes the experts, so the LLM adapts itself.
methods.results_note: On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, SVF beats LoRA on GSM8K (79.15 vs 77.18) and ARC-Easy while training less than 10% of LoRA's parameters.

relations.note: multiplicative instead of additive adjustment of singular values
far fewer parameters; experts can be mixed

methods.name: SVFT
methods.paper_title: SVFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Singular Vectors
methods.formula_latex: W=U(\Sigma+M)V^{\top}=W_0+UMV^{\top},\quad U,\Sigma,V\ \text{from the SVD of frozen } W_0,\ M\ \text{sparse with fixed pattern } \Omega\ \text{(plain/diagonal, banded, random, top-}k\text{)};\ \text{only } M_{\Omega} \text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer
methods.structure: sparse additive update in the singular-vector basis of W_0: Delta W = sum over (i,j) in Omega of m_ij u_i v_j^T, a fixed dictionary that depends on the weight rather than a free low-rank factorization. A diagonal Omega reduces it to a spectral shift.
methods.mergeable_reason: U M V^T is a fixed dense matrix after training.
methods.key_idea: Use the outer products of W_0's own singular vectors as a fixed dictionary and learn sparse coefficients for it, including off-diagonal ones. This trades parameters against expressivity smoothly.
methods.results_note: Recovers up to 96% of full fine-tuning performance while training 0.006-0.25% of parameters (e.g. Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B on GSM8K/MATH); baselines reach at most 85% with 0.03-0.8%.

relations.note: a diagonal mask gives SVDiff's spectral shift without the ReLU
weight-dependent fixed basis instead of learned low-rank factors

methods.name: OSF
methods.full_name: Orthogonal Subspace Fine-tuning (adaptive-SVD constrained full fine-tuning)
methods.paper_title: Sculpting Subspaces: Constrained Full Fine-Tuning in LLMs for Continual Learning
methods.locus: any linear layer (all-linear in LLMs)
methods.structure: splits W_0 along its singular spectrum into a frozen top-k subspace and a trainable complement. Gradient projection keeps every update orthogonal to the frozen principal subspace, and k is set per layer from an input-output similarity score.
methods.mergeable_reason: The trained low-singular components are summed back into a single dense weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: the two SVD parts reconstruct W_0 at initialization.
methods.key_idea: For continual learning, freeze each weight's high-singular-value directions and let new tasks change only the orthogonal low-singular-value subspace, chosen adaptively per layer. This keeps full-rank capacity with little forgetting and no per-task parameters.
methods.results_note: Reports up to 7% higher average accuracy than O-LoRA on standard continual-learning benchmarks (T5-Large) and 48.4% average accuracy on TRACE with LLaMA-2-7B-Chat while preserving general ability and safety.

relations.note: both put adaptation in the minor singular subspace of W_0 (MiLoRA via LoRA initialization)
PSOFT adapts only inside the principal subspace; OSF freezes it and adapts its complement

methods.name: DoRA
methods.paper_title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=\operatorname{diag}(m)\,\frac{W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA}{\big\|W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\big\|_{row}},\quad m\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ m,B,A\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (commonly all attention and MLP projections)
methods.structure: polar-type (magnitude x direction) reparameterization: a rank-r additive update of the direction, then normalization of each output neuron's weight vector onto the unit sphere, then a learned diagonal magnitude. This is weight normalization applied to W_0 + BA. The paper's 'column-wise' norm refers to its transposed d x k convention; the official and HF code take one norm per output neuron.
methods.mergeable_reason: After training, diag(m) times the normalized (W_0 + BA) is a fixed dense matrix that replaces W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 and m = ||W_0|| (per output neuron), so W = W_0 exactly.
methods.key_idea: Split each weight into a magnitude and a direction, as weight normalization does. Learn the magnitude directly and the direction with LoRA. This reproduces the negative correlation between magnitude and direction changes seen in full fine-tuning, which LoRA lacks.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA at a similar parameter count, e.g. +3.7 points on LLaMA-7B commonsense reasoning, with gains on LLaVA visual instruction tuning and VL-BART image/video-text tasks.

relations.note: the direction is updated by a LoRA term
BiDoRA keeps DoRA's parameterization and changes the optimization to bi-level
DeLoRA normalizes inside the rank-r bottleneck instead of per neuron of W_0 + BA

methods.name: BiDoRA
methods.paper_title: BiDoRA: Bi-level Optimization-Based Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=\operatorname{diag}(m)\,\frac{W_0+BA}{\|W_0+BA\|_{row}};\quad \min_{m}\ \mathcal{L}_{val}\big(\mathcal{V}^{*}(m),m\big)\ \ \text{s.t.}\ \ \mathcal{V}^{*}(m)=\arg\min_{\mathcal{V}=\{B,A\}}\ \mathcal{L}_{tr}(\mathcal{V},m)+\gamma\sum_k\big\|(V_k+\Delta V_k)^{\top}(V_k+\Delta V_k)-I\big\|_F^2
methods.locus: any linear layer (as DoRA)
methods.structure: DoRA's magnitude-direction parameterization, with magnitude and direction optimized at different levels of a bi-level program (hypergradient for the magnitude) and an orthogonality regularizer on the direction
methods.mergeable_reason: Same final parameterization as DoRA, so it folds into a single dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: As DoRA: B = 0 and m = ||W_0|| per neuron.
methods.key_idea: Train DoRA's magnitude and direction asynchronously: the direction on the training split and the magnitude on a validation split via hypergradients, then refit the direction. This decouples the two further and reduces overfitting.
methods.results_note: Reports an 85.2 GLUE average on RoBERTa-base vs 84.6 for DoRA, a smaller train-test gap, and gains over DoRA on 14 NLU, NLG and token-classification datasets.

relations.note: same parameterization, bi-level training

methods.name: DeLoRA
methods.paper_title: DeLoRA: Decoupling Angles and Strength in Low-rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\frac{\lambda\,\|W_0\|}{r}\,B\,\Xi\,A,\quad \Xi=\operatorname{diag}\Big(\tfrac{1}{\|b_i\|\,\|a_i\|}\Big)_{i=1}^{r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \lambda\ \text{learnable};\ \|\Delta W\|_F\le\lambda\|W_0\|
methods.locus: any linear layer
methods.structure: rank-r additive update in which each of the r rank-one directions b_i a_i^T is normalized (pure 'angles') and the overall strength is a single learnable bound lambda ||W_0||/r. This is a magnitude-direction decoupling in the r-dimensional bottleneck rather than per neuron.
methods.mergeable_reason: The bounded rank-r update is a fixed matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Paper: subtract a copy of the randomly initialized update from the frozen weights (W_0 <- W_0 - Delta W_init), as in PiSSA/ETHER. HF PEFT default: B = 0.
methods.key_idea: Normalize each rank-one component of the LoRA update and scale the sum by a learnable bound lambda ||W_0||/r. This separates learning the angle from the adaptation strength and makes training robust to learning rate and long schedules. The method can be derived from either LoRA or ETHER+.
methods.results_note: Reports an 85.6 GLUE average on RoBERTa-base (vs 84.7 for LoRA), subject-driven generation on par with DoRA/LoRA, and the best average in LLaMA-2-7B instruction tuning among the methods compared.

relations.note: derived from ETHER+: its fixed distance bound becomes a learnable bound and the rank becomes arbitrary
normalized LoRA factors with a learnable norm bound
normalizes inside the r-dim bottleneck and bounds ||Delta W|| instead of normalizing columns of W_0 + BA

methods.name: PoLAR
methods.paper_title: PoLAR: Polar-Decomposed Low-Rank Adapter Representation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+X\,\Theta\,Y^{\top},\quad X\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r),\ Y\in\mathrm{St}(d_{in},r),\ \Theta\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r};\ \text{retraction-free landing field } \Gamma(X)=\psi(X)X+\lambda\nabla\mathcal{N}(X);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: any linear layer
methods.structure: rank-r additive update in polar form: two direction factors on Stiefel manifolds (orthonormal r-frames, i.e. points of O(d)/O(d-r)) and an unconstrained r x r scale/core matrix, optimized by Riemannian 'landing' without retractions
methods.mergeable_reason: X Theta Y^T is a fixed rank-r matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Theta_0 = 0, with X_0 and Y_0 drawn uniformly at random from the Stiefel manifolds.
methods.key_idea: LoRA updates collapse to a very low stable rank. Writing the update as two orthonormal direction frames times a free core, and training with GPU-friendly Riemannian landing, keeps the directions diverse and provably speeds up convergence on a canonical low-rank problem.
methods.results_note: Reports gains over LoRA on GLUE (DeBERTa-v3-base 88.94 vs 88.18), commonsense reasoning (Llama-2-7B, 73.71 vs 72.18) and math (Gemma-3-27B) across models from 350M to 27B parameters.

relations.note: the same rank-r update, polar-decomposed
orthogonality over the whole factor instead of DoRA's per-neuron normalization
an SVD-shaped P Lambda Q update, with hard Stiefel constraints instead of an orthogonality penalty

methods.name: RoAd
methods.paper_title: 3-in-1: 2D Rotary Adaptation for Efficient Finetuning, Efficient Batching and Composability
methods.formula_latex: W=R\,W_0,\quad R=\operatorname{diag}(R_1,\dots,R_{d_{out}/2}),\ R_i=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_i\cos\theta_i&-\alpha_i\sin\theta_i\\ \alpha_i\sin\theta_i&\alpha_i\cos\theta_i\end{pmatrix};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (\alpha_i,\theta_i)\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: output representation of any linear layer
methods.structure: left action of the conformal group CO(2)^{d_out/2}, isomorphic to (C^x)^{d_out/2}: output coordinates are paired into complex numbers and each pair is multiplied by alpha e^{i theta} (RoAd_1). RoAd_2 and RoAd_4 untie the scales and angles inside each 2x2 block. The paper's z = R h implementation pairs element j with element j + group_size/2.
methods.mergeable_reason: The paper notes R folds into the weights (W_0 R^T in its transposed convention), with no inference overhead.
methods.identity_at_init: alpha_i = 1 and theta_i = 0.
methods.key_idea: Pilot studies show that fine-tuning mostly changes the angle of representations, not their magnitude, so RoAd learns scaled 2D rotations of paired output features. The element-wise form batches heterogeneous adapters efficiently and fits the distributed interchange intervention framework for composition and interpretability.
methods.results_note: Matches or beats other PEFT methods on GLUE, eight commonsense reasoning tasks and arithmetic reasoning with <0.1% trainable parameters (about 0.02% for commonsense), and about twice LoRA's throughput on heterogeneous batches.

relations.note: theta = 0 reduces RoAd to IA3-style output scaling (scales tied within pairs for RoAd_1, untied for RoAd_4)
both are framed as representation interventions; RoAd's intervention is an element-wise rotation
both act with 2x2 blocks; qGOFT on the input side with butterfly mixing, RoAd on fixed output pairs

methods.name: (IA)³
methods.full_name: Infused Adapter by Inhibiting and Amplifying Inner Activations
methods.paper_title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
methods.formula_latex: W_k=\operatorname{diag}(l_k)\,W_k^{0},\quad W_v=\operatorname{diag}(l_v)\,W_v^{0},\quad W_2=W_2^{0}\operatorname{diag}(l_{ff})\ \ \big(\text{i.e. } (l_{ff}\odot\gamma(W_1x))W_2\big);\ \text{all } W^{0}\ \text{frozen},\ l_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_k},\ l_v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_v},\ l_{ff}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{ff}}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: L(d_k+d_v+d_{ff})\ \text{per model, i.e. } d_{out}\ \text{per key/value projection and } d_{ff}\ \text{per FFN}
methods.locus: keys and values in every attention block, and the inner FFN activation (input of the down-projection)
methods.structure: diagonal scaling: a left action of the torus (R^x)^{d_out} on the rows of W_k and W_v, and a right action of (R^x)^{d_ff} on the columns of the FFN down-projection
methods.mergeable_reason: Each diag(l) multiplies directly into the corresponding frozen weight matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: All l vectors are initialized to ones.
methods.key_idea: Learn only element-wise rescaling vectors that inhibit or amplify keys, values and FFN activations. With the T-Few recipe (unlikelihood and length-normalized losses, multitask pre-training of the vectors), this beats in-context learning at a fraction of the inference cost.
methods.results_note: T-Few with (IA)³ on T0-3B reaches 75.8% on RAFT, the first result above the human baseline (73.5%), training about 0.01% of the parameters.

relations.note: diagonal multiplicative scaling vs low-rank addition
the FLoRA paper describes IA3 as a 'rank 0.5' FLoRA that rescales only columns
same per-channel scaling idea; SSF adds a shift and targets vision backbones
GLoRA's multiplicative support with a vector parameterization gives diag(1+a) W_0

methods.name: SSF
methods.paper_title: Scaling & Shifting Your Features: A New Baseline for Efficient Model Tuning
methods.formula_latex: y=\gamma\odot x+\beta\ \text{after each operation (MSA, MLP, LayerNorm)};\ \text{after a linear op: } W=\operatorname{diag}(\gamma)\,W_0,\ b=\gamma\odot b_0+\beta;\ W_0,b_0\ \text{frozen},\ \gamma,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: after every operation of a ViT block (attention, MLP, LayerNorm)
methods.structure: a per-channel affine map (diagonal scaling plus shift), i.e. an action of the diagonal affine group (R^x)^d semidirect R^d on output channels, re-parameterizable into the preceding linear layer
methods.mergeable_reason: The paper re-parameterizes (gamma, beta) into the preceding linear/conv weight and bias, so inference runs the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: gamma ~ N(1, sigma) and beta ~ N(0, sigma): close to, but not exactly, the identity.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning a pretrained vision backbone can be reduced to learning a per-channel scale and shift of its features. These fold back into the weights, so there is no inference overhead.
methods.results_note: With ViT-B/16, reports 90.72% on FGVC and 73.10% on VTAB-1k (about 0.3M trainable parameters), above full fine-tuning (88.54% and 65.57%).

relations.note: per-channel scaling, plus a shift, for vision models
SSF's shift is a bias update; SSF adds a multiplicative scale
GLoRA reports SSF as a special case of its unified formulation

methods.name: RED
methods.paper_title: Advancing Parameter Efficiency in Fine-tuning via Representation Editing
methods.formula_latex: h_2=l_{scaling}\odot h_1+l_{bias},\ h_1=\text{output of each FFN sub-layer};\ \text{equivalently } W_{down}=\operatorname{diag}(l_{scaling})\,W_{down}^{0},\ b=l_{scaling}\odot b^{0}+l_{bias};\ \text{model frozen},\ l_{scaling},l_{bias}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: outputs of the FFN sub-layer in every Transformer layer (ablations also edit Q, K, V)
methods.structure: per-channel affine edit (diagonal scaling plus shift) of each FFN's contribution to the residual stream; the same algebraic form as SSF, applied to LLM FFN outputs
methods.mergeable_reason: The scaling always folds into the FFN down-projection; the shift folds into its bias only if that layer has one (LLaMA-style down-projections have no bias, so a bias term must be added).
methods.identity_at_init: l_scaling = 1 and l_bias = 0.
methods.key_idea: Instead of adding modules, edit hidden representations directly with one scaling vector and one bias vector per layer. This uses about 25,700x fewer parameters than full fine-tuning and about 32x fewer than LoRA, with no rank to tune.
methods.results_note: Comparable to or better than full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods on GLUE (RoBERTa, T5), E2E NLG (GPT-2) and LLaMA-2 instruction tuning (AlpacaEval) with far fewer parameters.

relations.note: same scale-and-shift form applied to LLM FFN outputs
IA3 scales keys/values/FFN activations without a shift
both edit representations; RED's edit is a diagonal affine map

methods.name: LN Tuning
methods.paper_title: Tuning LayerNorm in Attention: Towards Efficient Multi-Modal LLM Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{LN}(x)=g\odot\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}+b,\ \text{only } (g,b)\ \text{of the attention-block LayerNorms trained};\ \text{equivalently } W=W_0\operatorname{diag}(g/g_0)\ \text{for the linear map that follows, plus a bias shift}
methods.locus: LayerNorm gains and biases in every attention block (input and post-attention LayerNorm)
methods.structure: selective tuning of existing per-channel gains, which equals a diagonal scaling of the input of the next linear map (a right action of (R^x)^d on W_0) plus a shift
methods.mergeable_reason: The tuned LayerNorm parameters simply replace the old ones; no modules are added.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained LayerNorm parameters (exact identity).
methods.key_idea: Treat turning an LLM into a multimodal LLM as domain adaptation. For that, tuning only the LayerNorm gains and biases inside attention blocks is enough.
methods.results_note: At 13B scale, beats LoRA by over 20% on average across five multimodal benchmarks with 41.9% fewer trainable parameters and 17.6% less GPU memory.

relations.note: both rescale channels; LN tuning reuses existing gains instead of adding vectors
selective tuning of a tiny existing parameter subset
main baseline in the paper

methods.name: DiffFit
methods.full_name: DiffFit (bias tuning plus learnable residual scaling for diffusion transformers)
methods.paper_title: DiffFit: Unlocking Transferability of Large Diffusion Models via Simple Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: x\leftarrow x+\gamma_1\odot\mathrm{Attn}(x),\quad x\leftarrow x+\gamma_2\odot\mathrm{FFN}(x),\ \gamma_1,\gamma_2\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ (\text{init } \mathbf{1});\ \text{trained: } \gamma,\ \text{biases, normalization parameters, class embedding; all other weights frozen}
methods.locus: residual branches of DiT blocks (the first 14 blocks of DiT-XL/2), plus all biases, norms and the class embedding
methods.structure: diagonal scaling of each residual branch's output (foldable into the branch's output projection) combined with BitFit-style selective tuning of biases and normalization parameters
methods.mergeable_reason: gamma folds into the output projection weight and bias of the attention/FFN branch; the tuned biases and norms replace the old ones.
methods.identity_at_init: gamma = 1, and biases and norms start from their pretrained values.
methods.key_idea: For diffusion transformers, tuning the biases plus a learnable per-channel scale on each residual branch is enough to transfer quickly to new domains and resolutions.
methods.results_note: About 2x faster training than full fine-tuning, storing about 0.12% of the parameters; FID 3.02 on ImageNet 512x512 after 25 epochs from a 256x256 checkpoint.

relations.note: bias tuning plus added scaling factors
per-channel scaling of features in vision transformers

methods.name: HiRA
methods.paper_title: HiRA: Parameter-Efficient Hadamard High-Rank Adaptation for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+W_0\odot(BA)=W_0\odot(\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}+BA),\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ B,A\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (LLM attention and MLP projections)
methods.structure: entry-wise (Hadamard) multiplicative modulation of W_0 by J + BA. Delta W = W_0 ⊙ BA has rank <= rank(W_0)·r, so the update is high-rank at LoRA's parameter cost. LoRA is recovered by replacing W_0 with the all-ones matrix.
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 + W_0 ⊙ BA is precomputed for deployment; the original weight can be recovered by element-wise division by 1 + BA.
methods.identity_at_init: One factor is zero (the paper zero-initializes its d x r factor and Kaiming-initializes the other), so Delta W = 0.
methods.key_idea: Multiply the pretrained matrix element-wise by a low-rank matrix. The Hadamard product with W_0 raises the possible rank of the update (up to rank(W_0)·r) without extra parameters and carries the pretrained structure into the update.
methods.results_note: Reports gains over LoRA and other PEFT baselines on commonsense reasoning with Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B, plus further generation tasks, at LoRA's parameter count (ICLR 2025 oral).

relations.note: with W_0 replaced by the all-ones matrix, HiRA's update is LoRA's BA
GLoRA's official code already implements W_0 + W_0 ⊙ A + B; HiRA is the case of a low-rank A and B = 0
LieRA's first-order approximation W_0 + W_0 ⊙ Delta W is exactly HiRA
both modulate W_0 entry-wise by a low-rank matrix; HiRA's J + BA has rank <= r+1

methods.name: LieRA
methods.full_name: Lie-group Rank Adaptation (Lie-group-based generalized tensor PEFT)
methods.paper_title: Generalized Tensor-based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Lie Group Transformations
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0\odot\exp_{\odot}(\Delta W)\approx W_0+W_0\odot\Delta W,\quad \Delta W=BA\ (\text{or a low-rank tensor for conv kernels}),\ \exp_{\odot}\ \text{entry-wise};\ W_0\ \text{frozen (non-zero entries)},\ B,A\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: linear layers and higher-order (convolutional) kernels
methods.structure: action of the abelian Lie group of entry-wise non-zero tensors under the Hadamard product (identity = all-ones tensor) on W_0. The update lives in its Lie algebra (all real tensors) and is mapped back through the entry-wise exponential; truncating at first order gives W_0 + W_0 ⊙ Delta W.
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 ⊙ exp(BA) is a fixed tensor of the original shape after training.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (A Gaussian), so exp(0) = 1 and W = W_0.
methods.key_idea: Treat parameters as elements of a Lie group under element-wise multiplication. Matrix PEFT updates (LoRA-style) then lift to high-dimensional (conv) tensors without flattening, via the exponential map from the Lie algebra.
methods.results_note: Reports gains over LoRA, e.g. 75.5 vs 74.1 on VTAB-1K (r=16), plus improvements on COCO detection, LLaMA-7B commonsense reasoning and GLUE.

relations.note: the first-order approximation equals HiRA's W_0 + W_0 ⊙ BA
Delta W in the Lie algebra is LoRA-factorized

methods.name: FLoRA
methods.full_name: Fast LoRA (batched, example-specific multiplicative low-rank adaptation)
methods.paper_title: Batched Low-Rank Adaptation of Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W_i=W_0\odot(B_iA_i),\quad h_i=\sum_{j=1}^{r}b^{(i)}_j\odot\big(W_0\,(a^{(i)}_j\odot x_i)\big),\ B_i=[b^{(i)}_1,\dots,b^{(i)}_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i^{\top}=[a^{(i)}_1,\dots,a^{(i)}_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{per example/adapter } i;\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: linear layers, with per-request adapters in multi-tenant serving
methods.structure: entry-wise (Hadamard) modulation of W_0 by a rank-r matrix. The rank-1 case is a two-sided diagonal scaling diag(b) W_0 diag(a), an action of the torus (R^x)^{d_out} x (R^x)^{d_in}; rank r is a sum of r such scalings, so a batch with different adapters needs only element-wise operations around one shared matmul.
methods.mergeable_reason: For a fixed adapter, W_0 ⊙ BA can be precomputed; the point of the method is to keep it unmerged so different examples in a batch can use different adapters.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the method section read. The parameterization reproduces W_0 only when B_iA_i is the all-ones matrix (e.g. rank-1 all-ones vectors), not with LoRA's B = 0.
methods.key_idea: Make each request's adapter multiply W_0 entry-wise. A minibatch with heterogeneous adapters can then be served with cheap element-wise operations around one shared matmul, giving better throughput and latency than batched LoRA.
methods.results_note: Improves throughput and latency over LoRA when serving heterogeneous adapters while keeping LoRA-level accuracy on multilingual code generation.

relations.note: the paper describes IA3 as a 'rank 0.5' special case that rescales only columns
same parameter count, multiplicative instead of additive, built for heterogeneous batching
HiRA's J + BA modulation is a FLoRA modulation of rank <= r+1

methods.name: GLoRA
methods.paper_title: One-for-All: Generalized LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+W_0\odot A+B,\quad b=b_0+b_0\odot D+E+W_0C;\ \text{each support } A,B,C,D,E\in\{\text{low-rank},\ \text{vector},\ \text{scalar},\ \text{none}\}\ \text{chosen per layer by evolutionary search};\ W_0,b_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \le 2r(d_{in}+d_{out})+r(d_{in}+1)+2d_{out}\ \text{(all supports low-rank or vector); per-layer configuration searched}
methods.locus: any linear layer (weights and biases) of ViTs and LLaMA models
methods.structure: a unified affine reparameterization that combines a Hadamard-multiplicative modulation of W_0 (W_0 ⊙ A), an additive update B, multiplicative and additive bias terms, and a weight-dependent 'prompt' bias W_0 C. Every term is linear in (W_0, b_0), so all of them fold into one weight and bias. The paper writes W_0 A as a product, but the official code and HF PEFT use the element-wise product.
methods.mergeable_reason: The paper's structural re-parameterization folds every support tensor into a single weight and bias, so inference has no extra cost.
methods.identity_at_init: Supports start at zero (one factor of each low-rank support is zero, vector/scalar supports are zero), so W = W_0 and b = b_0.
methods.key_idea: One supernet of re-parameterizable scaling and shifting terms on weights, biases and features covers LoRA-, SSF- and prompt-style tuning. An evolutionary search picks a configuration per layer, and everything merges back with no inference cost.
methods.results_note: Reports a 78.0% VTAB-1K average with 0.86M parameters (up to +2.9 points over prior PEFT methods), strong few-shot results, and gains over LoRA for LLaMA-1/2-7B on Open LLM Leaderboard tasks.

relations.note: the additive support B in low-rank form is LoRA
per-channel scaling and shifting via vector supports
a vector multiplicative support gives diag(1+a) W_0
a low-rank multiplicative support A with B = 0 is HiRA's W_0 + W_0 ⊙ BA

methods.name: PaRa
methods.paper_title: PaRa: Personalizing Text-to-Image Diffusion via Parameter Rank Reduction
methods.formula_latex: W=(I-QQ^{\top})\,W_0,\quad Q=\mathrm{qr}(B),\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained};\ W_0\ \text{frozen};\ \operatorname{rank}(W)\le\operatorname{rank}(W_0)-r\ \text{(Thm. 1)}
methods.locus: linear layers of the text-to-image diffusion UNet
methods.structure: left multiplication by an orthogonal projector onto the complement of a learned r-dimensional output subspace. This is an idempotent, non-invertible element of the matrix monoid rather than a group element; it removes r directions from the column space of W_0. Sequential application composes subjects: W_m = W_1 - Q_2 Q_2^T W_1.
methods.mergeable_reason: (I - QQ^T) W_0 is a fixed dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: No. Removing a rank-r projector changes W_0 from step 0; the HF PEFT docs state that the adapter is not the identity at initialization.
methods.key_idea: For personalization, shrink the parameter space instead of growing it. Explicitly lowering the rank of each weight, by projecting out a learned subspace, constrains the sampling trajectory toward the target concept while keeping text editability.
methods.results_note: Better target-image alignment than LoRA and SVDiff with about 2x fewer trainable parameters; human raters preferred PaRa in about 96-97% of single-subject comparisons.

relations.note: DEFT without the injection term (HF: DeftConfig(para=True))
rank reduction instead of a rank-increasing additive update; the two can be combined as W_0 - QQ^T W_0 + BA

methods.name: DEFT
methods.paper_title: DEFT: Decompositional Efficient Fine-Tuning for Text-to-Image Models
methods.formula_latex: W=(I-P_{proj})\,W_0+Q_PR,\quad P_{proj}=Q_PQ_P^{\top},\ Q_P=\mathrm{qr}(P)\ \ (\text{or } P_{proj}=P\,\mathrm{relu}(P)^{\top},\ Q_P=P),\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: linear layers of text-to-image (and unified image-generation) models
methods.structure: a projector (idempotent) left action that removes an r-dimensional output subspace from W_0, followed by an additive rank-r injection into exactly that subspace. The net update Q_P(R - Q_P^T W_0) has rank <= r.
methods.mergeable_reason: The HF docs state the update is a low-rank additive delta Q_P(R - Q_P^T W_0) that can be merged into the base weights.
methods.identity_at_init: R is initialized to Q_P^T W_0, so the removed component is re-injected and W = W_0 exactly (HF PEFT default).
methods.key_idea: Split the update into removing a low-rank subspace from the pretrained weight and injecting new content into that same subspace. Text-to-image models can then learn new concepts while keeping instruction following and editability.
methods.results_note: Reports state-of-the-art results on DreamBooth and DreamBench Plus personalization, InsDet object/scene adaptation and VisualCloze universal image generation.

relations.note: adds an injection term to PaRa's subspace removal and restores the identity at init
the injection is a rank-r additive term

methods.name: Quantum-PEFT
methods.full_name: Quantum-inspired PEFT with Pauli-parameterized unitary factors
methods.paper_title: Quantum-PEFT: Ultra parameter-efficient fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+U\Lambda V^{\top},\quad U=Q_{\mathsf P}(\theta_U)\,I_{d_{out}\times r},\ V=Q_{\mathsf P}(\theta_V)\,I_{d_{in}\times r},\ Q_{\mathsf P}=\text{product of } L \text{ layers of } R_Y\ \text{rotations and CZ gates on } \log_2 d\ \text{qubits},\ \Lambda\ \text{diagonal};\ \text{only } \theta_U,\theta_V,\Lambda\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer
methods.structure: a rank-r additive update in SVD shape whose orthonormal frames are images of a fixed frame under an orthogonal group element generated by a logarithmic-depth quantum-circuit (Pauli) parameterization. The Stiefel factors are orbits in a homogeneous space of O(d).
methods.mergeable_reason: U Lambda V^T is a fixed rank-r matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Delta W = U Lambda V^T vanishes when Lambda = 0; the paper's exact initialization was not confirmed.
methods.key_idea: Generate the orthonormal factors of an SVD-shaped adapter from a quantum-circuit (Pauli) parameterization of unitary matrices, so the number of trainable parameters grows only logarithmically with layer width.
methods.results_note: Reports about 25x fewer parameters than LoRA on DeBERTaV3-base GLUE (0.013M vs 0.33M) and 4.67x fewer on Mistral-7B, with competitive or better accuracy.

relations.note: logarithmic instead of linear parameter growth
both use Stiefel-frame x core factorizations; Quantum-PEFT generates the frames from a small Lie-group parameterization
both use an SVD-shaped P Lambda Q additive update

papers.title: Learning towards Minimum Hyperspherical Energy
papers.claim: Defines hyperspherical energy, a Thomson-problem-style potential of neurons on the unit sphere, as a measure of neuron diversity, and regularizes networks to minimize it.
papers.relevance: Hyperspherical energy is the invariant that OFT, BOFT, GOFT and HRA preserve. Orthogonal group actions are exactly the isometries that fix pairwise neuron angles, so orthogonal PEFT is fine-tuning inside an orbit that keeps this invariant.

papers.title: Orthogonal Over-Parameterized Training
papers.claim: Trains a network by learning an orthogonal transformation applied to fixed, randomly initialized neurons. This provably keeps the hyperspherical energy constant and improves generalization.
papers.relevance: Direct precursor of OFT: the trainable object is only a group element of O(d) acting on a frozen weight, which is the template for every multiplicative PEFT method.

papers.title: Weight Normalization: A Simple Reparameterization to Accelerate Training of Deep Neural Networks
papers.claim: Reparameterizes each weight vector as w = g v/||v||, separating magnitude from direction, which improves conditioning and speeds up SGD.
papers.relevance: The template for the magnitude-direction decompositions in DoRA, BiDoRA and DeLoRA: a polar-type factorization of each neuron into a radial scalar and a point on the sphere.

papers.title: FiLM: Visual Reasoning with a General Conditioning Layer
papers.claim: A feature-wise affine modulation (gamma ⊙ x + beta), predicted from a conditioning input, is a simple and general conditioning layer for neural networks.
papers.relevance: Feature-wise scale and shift is the algebraic building block behind (IA)³, SSF, RED, DiffFit and LN tuning: an action of the diagonal affine group on channels, learned as a static vector instead of predicted per input.

papers.title: Learning Fast Algorithms for Linear Transforms Using Butterfly Factorizations
papers.claim: Products of O(log n) sparse butterfly factors can represent and learn fast transforms (FFT, DCT, Hadamard, ...) with O(n log n) parameters.
papers.relevance: The structural basis of BOFT and of GOFT's parallel Givens layers: dense group elements written as short words in sparse generators, which is how multiplicative PEFT reaches dense rotations cheaply.

papers.title: Cheap Orthogonal Constraints in Neural Networks: A Simple Parametrization of the Orthogonal and Unitary Group
papers.claim: Parameterizes the special orthogonal and unitary groups through the exponential map from skew-symmetric (Lie-algebra) matrices, so optimization is unconstrained while orthogonality holds exactly.
papers.relevance: Supplies the Lie algebra to Lie group charts (exponential, Cayley) that OFT, BOFT, OFTv2, PSOFT and Spectral Adapter use. In these terms, multiplicative PEFT is gradient descent in a Lie algebra pushed forward to a group acting on W_0.

papers.title: Efficient Orthogonal Parametrisation of Recurrent Neural Networks Using Householder Reflections
papers.claim: Parameterizes orthogonal transition matrices as products of Householder reflections, which gives exact orthogonality and a tunable trade-off between the number of reflections and expressivity at low cost.
papers.relevance: The ancestor of HRA and ETHER: Householder words generate O(d), and word length controls capacity. HRA's 'r reflections = identity plus rank r' is the PEFT version of this fact.

papers.title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
papers.claim: LoRA and full fine-tuning reach structurally different solutions. LoRA introduces 'intruder dimensions' (new high-ranking singular vectors unlike the pretrained ones) that cause forgetting, and scaling them down recovers much of the pretraining behaviour.
papers.relevance: A spectral test that separates additive low-rank updates from updates that preserve the pretrained spectrum. It motivates methods such as SVF, SVDiff, PSOFT, OSF, Spectral Adapter and OFT that keep the singular frame of W_0.

papers.title: The Primacy of Magnitude in Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.claim: Argues that the magnitude of the weight update is the main driver of LoRA performance and that low-rank structure bounds it. Proposes LoRAM, a magnitude-driven initialization that matches spectral initializations without their SVD cost.
papers.relevance: Isolates the magnitude half of magnitude-direction decompositions (DoRA, DeLoRA, PoLAR) and suggests that many spectral or initialization gains come down to controlling update magnitude.

notes: Convention: all formulas use h = W x with W_0 of shape d_out x d_in. Many source papers (OFT, BOFT, GOFT, ETHER, RoAd, PSOFT) write z = (R W)^T x with W of shape d_in x d_out, so their 'left' rotation is a right action on W_0 here. Since R and R^T lie in the same group, these are rewritten as W = W_0 R (or W = W_0 R^T). The family splits into algebraic sub-types useful for a categorical treatment. (1) Orthogonal group actions on the input side: OFT, BOFT, OFTv2, GOFT, HRA, ETHER, and PSOFT / Spectral Adapter^R restricted to principal subspaces. (2) Actions that leave O(d): qGOFT (GL(2) blocks), ETHER+ (rank-2 perturbations), RoAd (CO(2) ≅ C^x on output pairs). (3) Diagonal torus actions on channels: (IA)³, SSF, RED, LN tuning, DiffFit. (4) Torus actions on the spectrum: SVDiff, SVF, SVFT-plain. (5) Entry-wise Hadamard group actions: FLoRA, HiRA, LieRA, the W_0 ⊙ A term of GLoRA. (6) Magnitude-direction (polar) decompositions: DoRA, BiDoRA, DeLoRA, PoLAR. (7) Non-invertible projector (monoid) actions: PaRa, DEFT. (8) Lie-group-generated frames for additive updates: Quantum-PEFT. Membership choices: PoLAR, DeLoRA, Spectral Adapter^A, SVFT and Quantum-PEFT are honestly additive-weight but are kept because their structure is a polar, spectral or group-generated decomposition; other families may also list them. OSF is a gradient-projection method in the singular basis (in HF PEFT). LN tuning is selective. Uncertainties: (a) HiRA has no arXiv version (ICLR 2025 oral, OpenReview TwJrTz9cRS); its year is recorded as 2025. (b) GLoRA's paper writes W_0 A (a matrix product), but the official code and HF PEFT use the Hadamard product W_0 ⊙ A. The entry follows the code; GLoRA has no confirmed peer-reviewed venue. (c) The ETHER/ETHER+ initialization is not stated clearly in the text read. A single Householder reflection cannot be the identity, while ETHER+ can be (u = v). (d) Transformer² SVF: the paper gives W' = U(Σ ⊗ diag(z))V^T, while the official code adds sigmoid(z) and a sum(σ)/sum(σz) renormalization, which is what makes initialization near-identity. (e) DoRA's paper calls its norm 'column-wise' in its transposed convention; the official and HF implementations use one magnitude per output neuron, which is what the formula shows. (f) FLoRA's identity-preserving initialization is not stated in the section read. (g) The PaRa and Quantum-PEFT initialization details are medium-confidence. (h) The OSF paper (Sculpting Subspaces) is listed as arXiv only, since no venue was confirmed. Excluded as low-uptake or out of scope: HOFT (Householder Orthogonal Fine-tuning, arXiv 2505.16531, no venue found), BoRA and EDoRA (DoRA variants), StelLA (Stiefel LoRA), and SVD-initialized additive methods (PiSSA, MiLoRA, KaSA, SORSA, LoRA-XS, TinyLoRA, AdaMSS, which belong with the additive/low-rank family). Relation targets outside this family use the assumed ids lora, qlora, pissa, milora, adalora, bitfit and loreft.
